q1_who.name: q1_who
q1_who.value: Diesel is a denim-led Italian fashion brand (founded 1978, Renzo Rosso) positioned explicitly as "the true alternative to luxury" — accessible-luxury / affordable-luxury tier, not mass. Under creative director Glenn Martens (since 2020) it has repositioned around denim, utility and Y2K pop aesthetics targeting a youth / digital-native audience. It is the founding brand of OTB Group (Breganze, Italy), alongside Maison Margiela, Marni, Jil Sander, Viktor&Rolf, plus Staff International (production/logistics, Dsquared2 licence), Brave Kid (kids licensees) and a stake in Amiri. Channel mix is shifting toward DTC: group retail/outlet/online now ~60% of turnover, with a sizeable but declining wholesale channel. Global footprint (~600 group directly-operated stores); strategic markets include Japan (27.4% of group business), North America, Middle East, plus new market entries (Mexico, Korea).

q2_direction.name: q2_direction
q2_direction.value: INNOVATING (brand); the group is playing efficiency catch-up. Trigger event = the 2020 appointment of Glenn Martens as creative director, which reset Diesel from an "impersonal", diluted 2010s denim label into a bold, youth-led, campaign-driven brand (first on-schedule Milan show 2021, livestreamed shows, free raves, It-bags like the 1DR). Editorial coverage documents a clear then-vs-now jump from heritage/impersonal denim toward irreverent, digital-native, campaign-style imagery over 2020–2025. NOTE: Wayback snapshot retrieval failed (tool timed out on two attempts), so the then-vs-now visual comparison is evidenced via dated editorial coverage rather than an archived snapshot — flag for human to pull an archive.org snapshot to confirm. Ongoing triggers: continued repositioning/rationalization, new market expansion (Mexico, Korea), and Martens now also leading sister-brand Margiela (halo effect). Live PDP audit shows the innovation is concentrated in campaigns while the PDP grid itself remains conventional clean-studio packshots — a gap Sartiq can close.

q5_pdp.name: q5_pdp
q5_pdp.value: MEASURED from live diesel.com PDP audits (sample across categories). Shots/SKU = 6 consistently (both a 1DR bag PDP and a 1995 denim PDP carried exactly 6 product images each). Image mix is category-dependent: APPAREL/denim is on-model heavy (~67% on-model, i.e. 4 of 6 worn shots on a model, plus 1 still-life + 1 detail), while ACCESSORIES/bags are still-life heavy (~67% still-life, with 1 on-model 'worn' shot + 1 detail). All images are shot on plain white studio backgrounds — clean, systematic, coherent packshot grid. NO video and NO lifestyle/campaign imagery observed on the PDPs themselves. Consistency is good at brand level (uniform white-background template), classifier flagged 'medium' within-set. Cross-channel note: wholesale partners (the declining channel) and sister maisons need the same consistent asset style at lower cost. Key insight: Diesel's campaign/brand energy is bold and youth-led, but the PDP grid stays conventional and studio-clean — a clear wedge for Sartiq (add on-model variety, video, and localized variants without studio cost).
